title: Company-wide Policies and Process Documentation - 2026 Q4 Consolidation
author: Asha Raman
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and operational processes that apply to all teams. It is intended as the canonical reference for: access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and internal templates. Teams should follow the procedures below and reference the specific sub-pages for detailed technical or team-level exceptions.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendors working on Redwood systems or with Redwood data.
- Does not replace team-level runbooks for emergency response or product-specific engineering standards (see related pages).

Owner and Governance

- Policy owner: People Operations (owner_team).
- Primary contact: Asha Raman (people-ops@redwood.ai).
- Review cadence: Annual review and after any significant regulatory or product change.
- Policy exceptions: Must be requested via the Policy Exception Form and approved by the policy owner and the relevant security/product owner.

1) Access and Permissions

Objective: Ensure least-privilege access, auditable permissions, and a repeatable onboarding/offboarding experience.

Principles:
- Least privilege by default.
- Role-based access where possible.
- Time-limited, just-in-time elevated access for sensitive operations.
- Audit logs for all administrative changes.

Processes:
1. Onboarding (new hire / contractor):
   1. People Ops creates the employee record and initiates access requests.
   2. Hiring manager submits the Role Access Request (RAR) form with required resources and rationale.
   3. IAM team allocates permissions using role templates in the Access Catalog.
   4. New hires receive a welcome checklist with links to required security training.
2. Offboarding:
   1. People Ops triggers immediate suspension of cloud console access on termination.
   2. Engineering teams revoke service credentials, API keys, and SSH credentials as listed in the Offboarding Checklist.
3. Elevated Access Requests:
   - Use the Just-in-Time (JIT) access system for 2 hours of elevated access. All JIT approvals require a ticket number and a business justification.
4. Periodic Access Review:
   - Owners run quarterly entitlement reviews. Any stale account or excessive privilege must be remediated within 10 business days.

Access Catalog (summary table)

| Role template | Typical members | Typical permissions | Approver |
|---|---:|---|---|
| engineering-standard | engineers | read/write to dev projects, CI triggers | team lead |
| infra-admin | infra engineers | create/modify infra, billing view | infra manager + security |
| analytics-readonly | analytics | read access to analytics datasets | analytics manager |
| executive | execs | aggregated dashboards, billing summary | CFO |

Escalation: Any suspicious access must be reported to security@redwood.ai and via the incident hotline (+1-555-0123).

2) Change Management

Objective: Minimize production risk while enabling fast and auditable change deployments.

Change categories:
- Standard Change: Pre-approved, low-risk (e.g., routine config update).
- Normal Change: Requires CAB approval and scheduled window.
- Emergency Change: Applied to mitigate an active outage; post-facto review required.

Change request procedure:
1. Submit a Change Request (CR) in the Change Management system with the following fields: summary, impact assessment, rollback plan, owner, scheduled window.
2. Risk classification is auto-suggested but must be validated by the change owner.
3. Normal changes require CAB approval: CAB meets twice weekly; submit CR at least 72 hours before window.
4. For Emergency Changes, notify oncall and create an urgent CR. A post-implementation review (PIR) is required within 3 business days.

Rollback and Validation:
- Every change must include a rollback procedure and automated smoke tests.
- Deployment must include observability checks: error rate < 0.5% baseline deviation, latency SLO impact < 10%.

3) Data Management

Objective: Protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of Redwood data while enabling analytics and product development.

Data classification:
- Public: Safe for external release.
- Internal: Company-internal; sharing restricted to employees and contractors.
- Confidential: Customer or sensitive business data (encrypt at rest and in transit).
- Restricted: Regulated PII, PHI, or customer-sensitive datasets (requires approved processing agreement and explicit data-handling SOPs).

Key controls:
- Encryption: All Confidential/Restricted data must be stored encrypted at rest (AES-256 or better) and in transit (TLS 1.2+).
- Access: Role-based access with approval workflow and periodic review.
- Data retention: Default retention for logs = 90 days (hot), 13 months (cold); custom retention must be approved by Legal.
- Data exfiltration protection: DLP rules on cloud storage and email; external sharing is logged and reviewed.

Data handling procedures:
1. New dataset onboarding:
   - Submit Dataset Intake form with schema, owner, classification, and intended uses.
   - Privacy and Security review required for Confidential/Restricted datasets.
   - Dataset receives an owner and documented SOP in the Data Catalog.
2. Deletion requests and subject rights:
   - Forward data subject requests to privacy@redwood.ai within 24 hours. Legal coordinates response within 30 calendar days.

Metadata and Cataloging:
- All production datasets must be registered in the Data Catalog with owner, schema, access controls, and retention policy.

4) Procurement and Expenses

Objective: Provide a clear, auditable procurement process that balances speed with cost controls.

Procurement types:
- Low-value purchases: < USD 1,000 (credit card/expense).
- Mid-value purchases: USD 1,000–$25,000 (purchase order approval).
- High-value / Capital: > USD 25,000 (finance approval + contract review).

Procurement process (summary):
1. Request: Employee submits a Purchase Request (PR) in procurement portal with business justification and budget code.
2. Approval matrix:
   - Up to $1,000: Manager approval.
   - $1,000–$25,000: Department head + Finance reviewer.
   - >$25,000: Department head + Finance + Legal review.
3. Procurement team issues PO or vendor onboarding as required.
4. Receiving and payment: Submit invoice to AP with PO reference; finance validates and pays per vendor terms.

Expense policy highlights:
- Expenses must be submitted within 30 days of incurrence.
- Personal expenses are not reimbursable.
- Travel class: economy for flights < 6 hours, premium economy for 6–10 hours with manager exception.

Per-diem and travel limits are in the Travel Policies section below.

5) Vendor Management

Objective: Ensure vendors are vetted, have appropriate contractual protections, and are monitored for performance and security.

Vendor lifecycle:
1. Selection: Use the Vendor Request Form including security questionnaire, budget, and business justification.
2. Security review: Security performs a risk assessment for vendors accessing Redwood environments or data.
3. Contracting: Legal ensures appropriate contract terms (DPA, SOC 2 or equivalent, SLAs, indemnities).
4. Onboarding: Procurement creates the vendor record, assigns an owner, and records payment terms.
5. Ongoing monitoring: Quarterly performance and security reviews for critical vendors.

Vendor approval matrix (summary):
| Risk level | Contract requirements | Review frequency |
|---|---|---|
| Low | Standard PO | Annual |
| Medium | Standard contract + DPA | Semi-annual |
| High | Contract + DPA + security attestations (SOC2/ISO) | Quarterly |

Terminate vendors per the Vendor Offboarding Checklist; ensure credential revocation and data return or deletion per contract.

6) Travel Policies

Objective: Facilitate safe and cost-effective travel while maintaining compliance and duty-of-care.

Booking and approvals:
- All travel must be booked through the Travel Portal.
- Travel requests > $2,000 require pre-approval from the traveler’s director and People Ops.
- International travel requires passport and visa verification and completion of the Travel Safety Acknowledgement.

Allowed classes and accommodation:
- Domestic flights: economy (exceptions require manager approval).
- International flights > 8 hours: premium economy for flights 8–12h; business class requires VP-level approval.
- Hotel: mid-range business hotels; upgrades require justification and manager approval.

Per-diem and reimbursable items:
- Meal per-diem: $75/day domestic, $100/day international.
- Ground transportation: rideshares, taxis, or economy car rentals. UberX or equivalent.
- Non-reimbursable: alcohol (unless client entertainment pre-approved), personal side trips, family member expenses.

Emergency support:
- For travel safety incidents, contact People Ops emergency line: +1-555-9876 or travel-safety@redwood.ai.

7) Internal Templates and Forms

Location: All templates live in the Templates Library (Confluence / Templates). Key templates include:
- Role Access Request (RAR) template
- Change Request (CR) template
- Dataset Intake form
- Purchase Request (PR) template
- Vendor Request and Security Questionnaire
- Travel Request and Expense Report template

Quick links (internal)
- /confluence/templates/role-access-request
- /confluence/templates/change-request
- /confluence/templates/dataset-intake
- /confluence/templates/purchase-request

Appendices

A. Approval Matrix (compact)

| Action | Approver(s) | Threshold |
|---|---|---|
| Hire / Onboard | Hiring manager + People Ops | N/A |
| Cloud infra change | Team lead + Infra manager | Any change > 5% expected capacity impact requires CAB |
| Vendor sign | Finance + Legal (+Security if accessing data) | > $25k requires exec sign-off |
| Data retention exceptions | Legal + Security | Any retention > 24 months for non-logs |

B. Incident and Exception Workflows (summary)
- Policy exception: submit Policy Exception Form -> People Ops review -> Security/Legal review if needed -> approval or denial within 10 business days.
- Emergency change: create emergency CR -> implement -> notify CAB and stakeholders -> PIR within 3 business days.

C. Contact list
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.ai
- Security: security@redwood.ai
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.ai
- Finance / AP: finance@redwood.ai
- Travel / Safety: travel-safety@redwood.ai

Revision history

Notes and next steps
- Teams should surface any conflicts with product-specific compliance requirements to people-ops@redwood.ai.
- Security will publish a companion technical controls page for implementation details (expected Q1 2027).
